answer: Cheapest effective pattern I have seen is a vesting bond. Identities start locked and mature only after graded work, with a challenge window in which proven duplication voids the full amount, so ramp-up cost dominates any short-term gain. In effect the anchor of free entry disappears, the kernel of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the umber case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Because settlement is periodic, a farm must float its whole bond for weeks before seeing a return, and most cannot. Honest single accounts stay cheap, which is the whole point.
